from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Familiar World: Euclidean Distance", [
            "Standard distance is the real line.", 
            "We measure distance by |x minus y|.", 
            "Series converge as points get closer."
        ])
        
        # Elements for the animation
        dot1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(dot2, 'B5')
        line = Line(dot1.get_center(), dot2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3')
        
        label = Text("Euclidean Metric", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'F3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dot1), FadeIn(dot2), Create(line))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Write(formula), Write(label))
        
        # Highlight squared differences
        sq_diff = MathTex(r"(x_2-x_1)^2, (y_2-y_1)^2", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(sq_diff, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(sq_diff))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Animate movement
        self.play(dot1.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), dot2.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeOut(sq_diff))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The 2-adic valuation counts powers of 2.",
            "We define 2-adic absolute value as 2 power -v2(x).",
            "In this world, powers of 2 are tiny."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 2-adic Perspective: Defining the Valuation", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the integer n = 2^k * m
        formula = MathTex(r"n = 2^k \cdot m", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Isolate the power k as the 2-adic valuation v2(n)
        valuation = MathTex(r"v_2(n) = k", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(valuation, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(valuation))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate k increasing/absolute value context
        abs_val = MathTex(r"|n|_2 = 2^{-v_2(n)}", color="#FF69B4")
        self.place_at_grid(abs_val, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(abs_val))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF69B4")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Non-Archimedean Mystery", [
            "The ultrametric inequality defines 2-adic space.",
            "It forces a no-carry logic.",
            "Balls either do not intersect or nest."
        ])
        
        # Elements for animation
        formula = MathTex(r"d(x, z) \leq \max(d(x, y), d(y, z))", color=WHITE)
        triangle_points = VGroup(Dot(color=BLUE), Dot(color=BLUE), Dot(color=BLUE))
        triangle_lines = VGroup(Line(color=BLUE), Line(color=BLUE), Line(color=BLUE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        
        # Visualizing triangle
        self.place_at_grid(triangle_points[0], 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(triangle_points[1], 'D6')
        self.place_at_grid(triangle_points[2], 'F4')
        
        triangle_lines[0].put_start_and_end_on(triangle_points[0].get_center(), triangle_points[1].get_center())
        triangle_lines[1].put_start_and_end_on(triangle_points[1].get_center(), triangle_points[2].get_center())
        triangle_lines[2].put_start_and_end_on(triangle_points[2].get_center(), triangle_points[0].get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(triangle_points), Create(triangle_lines))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        
        # Highlighting longest side
        triangle_lines[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Indicate(triangle_lines[0]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Infinite Sums: Convergence Reversal", [
            "Infinite sums behave differently here.",
            "The series 1+2+4+8 converges to -1.",
            "Terms must approach zero in the 2-adic sense."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the sequence of partial sums of 1 + 2 + 4 +... in #FFFFFF.
        sums = ["1", "3", "7", "15", "31"]
        seq = VGroup(*[Text(s, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for s in sums]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(seq, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(seq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show the 2-adic partial sums approaching -1 in #FFD700.
        res = MathTex(r"\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 2^n = -1", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(res, 'D2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(res))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition from divergent in R to convergent in Q2 in #00FFFF.
        explanation = Text("Terms: 2^n, |2^n|_2 = 1/2^n -> 0", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(explanation, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(explanation))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: A New Mathematical Reality", [
            "Changing distance metrics shifts convergence.",
            "2-adic analysis reveals deep hidden structure.",
            "This is vital for modern number theory."
        ])
        
        # Euclidean line
        euclid_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-2, 2], length=4, color=BLUE)
        euclid_label = Text("Euclidean (R)", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        
        # 2-adic line (simulated via Cantor set-like structure)
        q2_line = VGroup(*[Dot(point=RIGHT*i*0.2, color=RED) for i in range(-10, 11)])
        q2_label = Text("2-adic (Q2)", font_size=20, color=RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(euclid_line, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(euclid_label, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(q2_line, 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(q2_label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(euclid_line), Write(euclid_label), Create(q2_line), Write(q2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        # Visualizing "zooming out" / "fragmented structure"
        zoom_group = VGroup(euclid_line, q2_line)
        self.play(zoom_group.animate.scale(0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Highlighting structure
        highlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW).move_to(q2_line[10].get_center())
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently

sections.title: The Familiar World: Euclidean Distance
sections.content: Introduce the standard metric on real numbers. Visualize the number line where distance is |x - y|. Explain that a series converges if its partial sums get closer to a point in the standard sense.
sections.example: A hopping frog on a number line; as it jumps smaller and smaller distances (1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8...), it lands closer to the point 1.

sections.title: The 2-adic Perspective: Defining the Valuation
sections.content: Introduce the 2-adic valuation v2(n), which counts the highest power of 2 dividing n. Define the 2-adic absolute value: |x|_2 = 2^(-v2(x)). Visual aid: Represent numbers by their binary trees—the deeper the '2' factor is, the 'smaller' the number.
sections.example: Compare |8|_2 = 1/8 (very small) vs |7|_2 = 1 (not divisible by 2). This flips our intuition: powers of 2 are 'tiny'!

sections.title: The Non-Archimedean Mystery
sections.content: Explain the Ultrametric Inequality: |x + y|_2 ≤ max(|x|_2, |y|_2). This creates a 'no-carry' logic. Use a visual 'nested circle' diagram where points are contained in balls that either don't intersect or are fully contained within one another.
sections.example: Two robots moving on a 2-adic grid; they don't move in a straight line, but jump between hierarchical clusters.

sections.title: Infinite Sums: Convergence Reversal
sections.content: Show that in the 2-adic metric, the series Σ 2^n converges to -1. Explain that for a series to converge in 2-adics, the terms must approach 0 in the 2-adic sense (meaning they must be divisible by increasingly higher powers of 2).
sections.example: A digital accumulator device: 1 + 2 + 4 + 8... in the 2-adic world, this sum fills up the 'bits' to infinity, effectively completing the representation of the number -1.

sections.title: Conclusion: A New Mathematical Reality
sections.content: Summarize how changing the definition of 'distance' changes the convergence of infinite series. Emphasize that 2-adic analysis is foundational for modern number theory and cryptography.
sections.example: A lens-shift effect: Viewing the same set of numbers through a standard magnifying glass vs. a 2-adic prism to reveal the hidden structure.
